members.statement_original:
Given parameters $H\in(0,1)$ and $\eta>0$, on a rich enough probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal A,\mathbb P_{H,\eta})$, the price model takes the form
\[
\begin{cases}
S_t=S_0+\int_0^t\sigma_s\,dB_s,\\
\sigma_t^2=\sigma_0^2\exp(X_t),\\
X_t=\eta W^H_{\lfloor t\delta^{-1}\rfloor\delta},
\end{cases}\tag{4}
\]
where $(B_t)$ is a Brownian motion and $(W_t^H)$ is an independent fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$ and $\eta,\sigma_0>0$ are nuisance parameters. With no loss of generality, we further assume $\sigma_0^2=1$.

members.statement_original:
We now consider Model (1), with the same accompanying statistical experiment as in the previous section, but we do not require that the volatility process $(\sigma_t)$ is piecewise constant: we now have
\[
\sigma_t^2=\sigma_0^2\exp(\eta W_t^H),
\]
where $W^H$ is a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H$ and independent from $B$. We will write $\mathbb E_{H,\eta}$ for the expectation under the probability measure $\mathbb P_{H,\eta}$. Without loss of generality, we take $\sigma_0=1$. We assume that $(H,\eta)$ lies in a compact subset $\mathcal D$ of $(0,3/4)\times(0,\infty)$. The upper bound $H<3/4$ is a bit artificial and done mainly for technical purposes. It can be improved to $H<1$ using second-order increments, see Section 4.

members.statement_original:
The rate $v_n$ is said to be a lower rate of convergence for estimating $H$ over $\mathcal D$ in the experiment $\mathcal E^n$ if there exists $c>0$ such that
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\widehat H_n}\sup_{(H,\eta)\in\mathcal D}\mathbb P_{H,\eta}(v_n^{-1}|\widehat H_n-H|\ge c)>0,
\]
where the infimum is taken over all $\mathcal A^n$-measurable random variables $\widehat H_n$ (i.e. all estimators).

members.statement_original:
Let $b\ge1$ and $s\ge1$. Consider $\mathbf r\in\{1,\ldots,2S\}^s$ such that $\sum_i r_i=b$. If $b=1$, we write
\[
\mathfrak W^{H,\mathbf r}_{j,p,k,l}=2^{j+p}\int_{k2^{-j}+l2^{-j-p}}^{k2^{-j}+(l+1)2^{-j-p}}W_u^H\,du=\int_0^1 W^H_{k2^{-j}+(l+u)2^{-j-p}}\,du
\]
and if $b\ge2$, we write
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak W^{H,\mathbf r}_{j,p,k,l}&=\prod_{i=1}^s\frac{2^{j+p}}{r_i!}\int_{k2^{-j}+l2^{-j-p}}^{k2^{-j}+(l+1)2^{-j-p}}(W_u^H-W^H_{k2^{-j}+l2^{-j-p}})^{r_i}\,du\\
&=\frac1{\mathbf r!}\int_{[0,1]^s}\prod_{i=1}^s(W^H_{k2^{-j}+(l+u_i)2^{-j-p}}-W^H_{k2^{-j}+l2^{-j-p}})^{r_i}\,du
\end{aligned}
\]
where $\mathbf r!=\prod_{i=1}^s r_i!$. Define also $\mathfrak W^{H,\mathbf r}_{p,l}=\mathfrak W^{H,\mathbf r}_{0,p,0,l}$.

members.statement_original:
Recall that we set $m=n\delta_n$, which is assumed to be an integer. For $0\le i<\delta_n^{-1}$, we have
\[
\sum_{j=1}^m(S_{(im+j)/n}-S_{(im+j-1)/n})^2=\sigma_{i\delta_n}^2\sum_{j=1}^m(B_{(im+j)/n}-B_{(im+j-1)/n})^2,
\]
so that
\[
\widehat X_{i,n}=\log\left(\frac nm\sum_{j=1}^m(S_{(im+j)/n}-S_{(im+j-1)/n})^2\right)=\eta W^H_{i\delta_n}+\varepsilon_{i,n,m},
\]
where the $(\varepsilon_{i,n,m})_i$ are independent, each $\varepsilon_{i,n,m}$ being distributed as
\[
\bar\varepsilon_m=\log\left(m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m(\bar\xi_j)^2\right)
\]
for i.i.d. standard Gaussian $(\bar\xi_j)_j$. Therefore the random variable $n\delta_n\exp(\varepsilon_{i,n,m})$ has a chi-square law with $n\delta_n$ degrees of freedom.

members.statement_original:
Pick $\nu_0>0$. We obtain a family of estimators of $H$ by setting
\[
\widehat H_n=-\frac12\log\left[\frac{\widehat Q_{J_n^*+1,N-J_n^*-1,n}}{\widehat Q_{J_n^*,N-J_n^*-1,n}}\right]
\]
where the data-driven rule for selecting the energy level is given by
\[
J_n^*=\max\{2\le j\le N-1:\widehat Q_{j,N-j-1,n}\ge\nu_0 2^j n^{-1}\}
\]
with the convention that $J_n^*=2$ when this set is empty.

members.statement_original:
A first estimator of $(H,\eta)$ is defined by $(\widehat H_n^{(0)},\widehat\eta_n^{(0)})$, with
\[
\widehat H_n^{(0)}=\min\left(\max\left(-\frac12\log_2\left[\frac{\widehat Q_{J_n^*+1,N-J_n^*-1,n}}{\widehat Q_{J_n^*,N-J_n^*-1,n}}\right],H_-\right),H_+\right)
\]
with $J_n^*=\max\{j:\widehat Q_{j,N-j-1,n}\ge2^jn^{-1}\}$, and then
\[
\widehat\eta_n^{(0)}=\min\left(\max\left(\left(\frac{\widehat Q_{\widehat j_n,N-\widehat j_n,n}2^{2\widehat j_n\widehat H_n^{(0)}}}{\kappa_{N-\widehat j_n,1}(\widehat H_n^{(0)})}\right)^{1/2},\eta_-\right),\eta_+\right)
\]
where $\widehat j_n=\left\lfloor\frac1{2\widehat H_n^{(0)}+1}\log_2n\right\rfloor$. The projection onto $[H_-,H_+]\times[\eta_-,\eta_+]\supseteq\mathcal D$ guarantees the stability of the bias correction procedure.
